collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A friend tells a villager about a shortcut through the trees: take the shortcut, or stick to the path.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is walking to the far gardens. (friend) calls out, "Don't go round by the path! There's a shortcut through the trees. Turn left at the big rock, then right at the bent palm." (subject) has never heard of this shortcut, but (friend) seems very sure.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) turns left at the big rock. There are several bent palms. (subject.He/she) chooses one. An hour later (subject.he/she) emerges from the trees covered in leaves, somewhere (subject.he/she) has never seen. It's quite pretty, actually. (subject.He/she) gets to the gardens by lunchtime instead of breakfast. "How was the shortcut?" asks (friend) that evening. "Scenic," says (subject).

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (subject) waves, says thanks and takes the path anyway. (subject.He/she) gets there at the usual time. Later (subject.he/she) mentions the shortcut to someone else, who says, "Oh, (friend)'s shortcut? Nobody's ever found it. Not even (friend)." (subject) laughs all the way home.
